reason: Both conversations asked the right first question (what the smell is like and where) and, once told 'hot plastic, warm plug, buzzing', correctly ordered an immediate stop and unplug with no further use until checked. Conversation 2 went meaningfully further on the points that matter for this hidden truth: it gave 999/consumer-unit guidance for smoke or flames, practical food-relocation advice, and crucially told her to look up the make and model on the Electrical Safety First recall checker or manufacturer site, noting fridge-freezers have been recalled for exactly this fault, which maps directly onto the Beko safety notice and the expected escalation path. Conversation 1 never raised recalls, make, model or age, and its first reply mislabelled the burning case as needing only an 'electrician' check alongside the drain checks. Conversation 2's one weakness was the long first reply suggesting she pull the fridge out, but that was framed only for a rotten-smell scenario and did not harm the outcome.
